adversarial.description: Static adversarial comparison of .agent/contracts/130.json against the feature 130 acceptance list, feature 129 preservation, methodology section 9, the product-variance record, and the two round-1 rejection causes. Searched the contract for duplicated or missing acceptance commands, an affirmative pass claim, a sixth feature 129 source attempt, an installed .nizam edit, full-live or seventeen-row/thirteen-case ownership inside feature 130, a raise of 7350 or 9555, illustrative Lisp forms treated as a launcher, a fresh process treated as a fresh build, empty environment variables treated as sufficient, implementation_obligations.cases, proposal_basis.circuit_breaker_130_contract_attempts, and NIP-0003 scenario assignments to cases 7, 10, 11, or 12. Verification commands are named runner checks, not negated greps or unpinned sorts. The twelve acceptance commands were not executed.
adversarial.result: No blocking defect. Each of the twelve feature-list commands is one verification command. Case requirements name the command and case number only. The removed round-1 keys are absent.

static_checks.criterion: Section 9 obligations are stated without treating illustrative Lisp forms as a tested launcher, a fresh process as a fresh build, or empty environment variables as sufficient.
static_checks.evidence: implementation_obligations and the named check requirements state git archive of committed source compiled afresh, fresh sbcl --no-sysinit --no-userinit --non-interactive, private HOME and XDG locations, a newly created empty private ASDF output directory, explicit CL_SOURCE_REGISTRY and ASDF_OUTPUT_TRANSLATIONS configurations that each contain :ignore-inherited-configuration and use private roots, toolchain lock and core provenance including the profile clean core and pinned toolchain, distinct ASDF no-op and genuine failure controls, and must_fail for unsaved definitions, a fasl compiled against an unsaved macro, inherited fasl or shared build cache, and a deleted definition that survives only in a development image. The three distortions are explicitly denied.
No object key named cases exists. The text circuit_breaker_130_contract_attempts does not occur. Round 1 required both removals.

static_checks.criterion: Cases 7, 10, 11, and 12 are not assigned unsourced NIP-0003 scenarios.
static_checks.evidence: The four case requirements say only that the command is the feature 130 acceptance command for that case number and that the proposal does not claim the check already passes. The contract text contains no NIP-0003, handoff, fixture, or scenario narrative. must_fail is not mapped to a case number. The case matrix records those four commands with owner 130 and no scenario.
jsonschema 4.26.0 Draft 2020-12 reported zero errors. status is proposed. approvals.revisions is 1. validator_mode_a and evaluator_contract_review remain false. approved_at is absent.

observations: Each of the twelve command strings also appears in the acceptance_test field of the same verification entry. That is one entry whose acceptance test text is the command, not a second acceptance command. The verification command list contains each command once.

verification also names bash tools/validate.sh and bash tools/validate.sh --payload once each, labeled as repository compliance and not as feature 130 acceptance tests. They do not replace the twelve commands, do not authorize an installed .nizam edit, and do not adopt feature 132 live-readiness.

Section 9 also says to load the new products, execute the recorded tests, and verify actual dependency resolution and emitted or loaded artifact paths. The recorded tests are the twelve commands, and compile-afresh is stated. Load and artifact-path verification are not separate contract sentences. They are not acceptance criteria in the feature list or the feature 130 architecture paragraph, and they are not rejection items.
The contract leaves validator_mode_a and evaluator_contract_review false. This review does not edit the contract, run state, or product files.
Mode A round 2 was read. Its prose was not the approval basis. The contract bytes match the sha256 recorded in .agent/validator/130-mode-a-r2.json.

Working-tree feature 130 differs from HEAD only by status pending to in_progress. The architecture paragraph and the twelve acceptance commands are unchanged. The contract does not repeat the historical pending claim.

final_verdict.summary: Approve proposed contract 130 revision 1. The twelve feature 130 acceptance commands are present once each and are not claimed to pass. Feature 129 stays intact, attempt 6 and installed .nizam edits stay unauthorized, and full-live plus the seventeen-row/thirteen-case matrix stay on features 131 and 132. The product variance is 1218 counted, headroom 632, estimate 750, excess 118, without raising 7350 or 9555. Section 9 obligations are stated without treating the illustrative Lisp forms as a launcher, a fresh process as a fresh build, or empty environment variables as sufficient. implementation_obligations.cases and proposal_basis.circuit_breaker_130_contract_attempts are gone, and cases 7, 10, 11, and 12 have no unsourced NIP-0003 scenario. issues, missing_acceptance_coverage, and unsupported_claims are empty. The twelve acceptance commands were not executed.
